chunks: And Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan عليه السلام:
asking him about salat (prayer) in crimson-dyed cloth, for indeed our companions avoid praying in it.
So he wrote: “There is no problem with it at all, and all praise is due to Allah.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابَنَا: our companions, referring to the Shia associates mentioned by the questioner
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being asked about
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: praise, here in the phrase of praising Allah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.يَتَوَقَّوْنَ: they avoid or are cautious about

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in crimson-dyed clothing according to Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal inquiry to Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about performing salat (prayer) in crimson-dyed garments. The Imam replies that there is no objection to it whatsoever, establishing its permissibility despite the caution shown by some companions.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.810 - Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar wrote to Abu Muhammad Imam Hasan ibn Ali (as),
asking about praying in garments dyed with crimson (qirmaz), saying, "Our companions avoid praying in it."
The Imam wrote back: "There is no problem with it at all, and all praise is due to Allah (swt)."
